Definition: of Latin origin; Rhegium, a place in Italy:--Rhegium.
BiblicalUsage: From Syracuse they fetched a compass and came to Rhegium, and after one day the south wind blew and they came the next day to Puteoli, on Paul's voyage to Rome. The south wind blew the next day, and the ship reached Puteoli on the last leg of the voyage.
TheologicalSignificance: I take it that the ports of Paul's voyage are named because the road to Rome was walked, not wished.
